newsitem.title: TAIWAN: HK people need Taiwan work permits after handover.
newsitem.headline: HK people need Taiwan work permits after handover.

text.p: Hong Kong and Macau people will need permits to work in Taiwan after the handover of the British and Portugese enclaves to China in July 1997 and December 1999, respectively, labour officials said on Tuesday.

"Under our plan, Hong Kong and Macau people would have to apply for work permits in order to work in Taiwan after the handover," a spokesman of the cabinet's Labour Affairs Council told Reuters by telephone.
Currently, people from Hong Kong and Macau are treated as equivalents of Taiwan nationals and do not need work permits, the official said.

He said the new requirement was in line with the government's Hong Kong-Macau Relations Act, passed by parliament on March 18 to govern Taiwan's trade and other activities with the two territorites after the Chinese takeover.

Hong Kong will revert to Chinese sovereignty on July 1, 1997, after more than 150 years of British colonial rule. The enclave of Macau will be handed back to the mainland on December 20, 1999, ending Portuguese control since 1557.

After the handover, Taiwan, which has remained a bitter rival to China since a civil war split them in 1949, would treat the two territories as special administrative areas and maintain its current operations there, officials have said.
Taiwan bans direct official contacts with mainland China.
